content:
Hi everyone,
I’m considering a project to formalize the Müntz–Szász theorem, i.e. the density of the span of the sparse monomials x ↦ x^λ in C under the usual divergence condition on the sum of 1/λ.
I couldn’t find this result in the mathlib4 documentation or on the undergrad TODO pages. Before I start, I’d like to check:

  • Is anyone already working on this?
  • Do you think this is an appropriate target for mathlib (in terms of scope and maintainability)?
    Thanks in advance for any guidance!

It's in the 1000 list and seems to be missing.
FWIW we do have Stone-Weierstrass

Thanks for the pointers! Since Müntz–Szász is on the 1000+ list, missing in mathlib, and Stone–Weierstrass is already there, I’d really like to try working on it.

I’m extremely new to Lean and mathlib (I’ve only done some basic tactics and small exercises so far), so I want to check what the right procedure is:

  • Should I already create a GitHub issue describing the project and then start with very small PRs (e.g., just definitions and tiny lemmas)?

  • Or would you recommend that I first do a smaller “training” project before attempting Müntz–Szász?
    Also, just to confirm: there is no deadline or time pressure for something like this, right? So sorry that I expect this will take me a while as I learn the library.
    Any advice on how to structure this as a newcomer would be very welcome
Don't think about mathlib for now. Just make a project and try proving the theorem.
Agree, proving a theorem and upstreaming it to Mathlib are concerns that can be surprisingly uncorrelated sometimes!
Thanks so much, that makes sense. I’ll set up a separate project and just try to prove the theorem there first.
